title: RoleCDE: Benchmarking and Mitigating Role–Alignment Trade-offs in Role-Playing Agents

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model decision-making in 'RoleCDE', a benchmark consisting of 24k dilemma scenarios where role-specific values (e.g., profit maximization) conflict with general alignment-oriented constraints (e.g., legality, ethics). The paper measures the 'Decision Bias Ratio' (DBR) to quantify the model's tendency to favor general alignment over character-specific values.

Analyzing how decision-making tendencies vary across eight semantic role categories, such as 'Business & Finance', 'Authority & Governance', and 'Care & Service', to determine if certain professional or social identities are more prone to 'Role-Value Decoupling'.

Assessing whether role-playing agents systematically default to morality-consistent decisions rather than role-specific values when the two are in direct opposition, even under explicit character conditioning.
